SUMMARY:
• He stays the same man. All 9 locked photos score 0.72 to 0.84 against his age-22 photo, well over the 0.4 line. The GAN proof ranged 0.39 to 0.88 and lost Meza at 34.
  • Far more lifelike. Real skin, light, jerseys and pads in the right team colours. Logos and numbers are garbled, as expected.
  • Ageing is too weak. The lock copies the age-22 face so closely that 17 and 34 look much like 22. An age reader puts the photos at 25 to 36 (the GAN read 24 to 42). McSpadden's hairline does not recede at 28 or 34.
  • Weight barely shows. Prude at 268 lb and at 320 lb has nearly the same face, for the same reason.
  • Beards follow the description. Prude is light at 17 and full from 28; Meza keeps his goatee.
  • Same pose every time. The lock also copies head position, so a career of photos looks like one sitting.
  • Weakening the lock lets age and weight show but costs likeness. I tried three strengths on Prude at 28: full strength scored 0.84 but copied the gray jersey of an earlier age-22 photo instead of drawing the Ravens one; the setting used here scored 0.75 and took the Ravens jersey.

Measured on: a cloud machine with 4 Intel Xeon cores at 2.8 GHz, 15 GB memory and no graphics card. Every time is per 896 by 1152 photo, including decoding the picture. The Mac numbers are estimates, not measured. The M1 would run the model on its built-in graphics chip, which is usually several times faster than these 4 cores for this kind of model; the Intel Mac would run on its processor, likely slower than this cloud machine (no AVX-512 on most Mac chips, laptop cooling).

Memory and disk: the model files are about 11 GB on disk. Drawing a locked photo needed about 10 GB of memory here even with tricks. An 8 GB M1 would swap to disk and slow down a lot; a 16 GB M1 should be fine.

What it means in the game (estimate): drawing faces ahead of time for everyone is out of reach. At about 3 min a locked photo on an M1, 100 new faces take about 5 hours. It could work only on demand, drawing a player the first time you open his page (a few minutes of waiting, or in the background), and redrawing every 4 years on media day per the design.
LIGHT:
The second row of each player uses a model a generation older and about a third the size: Realistic Vision 6 (Stable Diffusion 1.5) at 512 by 640, sped up to 8 steps (Hyper-SD), with the IP-Adapter FaceID Plus v2 face lock.

  • Still the same man, but less firmly. The 9 locked photos score 0.52 to 0.71 against age 22 (the big model got 0.72 to 0.84). Every photo is over the 0.4 line.
  • Ages a little better. Since the lock is looser, McSpadden looks like a boy at 17 and older at 34.
  • Clearly rougher. Framing and hair wander between photos: Prude has long hair at 17 and 28 and headphones at 34, even with "short hair" in the description. Some jerseys come out in the wrong colours. Skin and light are less polished.
  • It took tuning. The first try drew Prude as a woman, and the first locked photos were blotchy. I rewrote the prompts and tried three lock settings on Prude; the 8-step, low-guidance one was cleanest. McSpadden's age-22 photo was redrawn twice (long hair holding the ball, then a helmet).
